title: the mountain of herbs
hook: a night flight the length of India, and herbs that hide

segments.voice: Yesterday: Lakshmana wounded, the army fallen, and Jambavan, blind with arrows, asking first whether Hanuman was alive. Did you ask who could still act? Tonight, Hanuman goes. Day six hundred forty-nine.

Hanuman climbs a mountain at the edge of the sea to push off, and he grows, the way he grew before the first leap. He presses down with his feet and the mountain buckles under him. Then he's in the air, heading north. This isn't the hop to Lanka. This is the whole length of India, there and back, before dawn, with the army lying in the dark behind him.

Valmiki lets us ride along. Below him slide the ocean, then the forests, rivers and towns, the hermitages of sages, the land unrolling under a flying monkey at night. Then the Himalaya rise ahead, snow and gold and rock. He sees Kailasa, the home of Shiva. He sees Mount Rishabha. And between them, just as Jambavan said, the mountain of herbs, glowing with its plants. Then comes the twist. Hanuman searches the slopes, and he can't find the four herbs. Valmiki says the plants knew someone had come for them, and they hid. They made themselves invisible. Think how that would feel: you've crossed half the world, the clock is running, and the thing you came for won't let itself be found. Hanuman won't spend the rest of the night searching. He gets angry, and he speaks to the mountain. You won't help Rama? Then see what happens. He grips the whole peak, with its trees, its animals, its glowing herbs, tears it loose, and lifts it into the sky. And he flies south with it, Valmiki says, shining like a second sun. If you've grown up seeing Hanuman's picture, this is the one: a monkey in flight, a mountain held up on one hand. It began with a plant that wouldn't be found, and a messenger who decided not to choose. If I can't find the one thing, he reasons, I'll bring everything.
screen: `THE LENGTH OF INDIA AT NIGHT.` · `KAILASA AND RISHABHA.` · `THE HERBS HIDE.` · `HE LIFTS THE WHOLE PEAK.` · then, large: `IF I CAN'T FIND IT, I'LL BRING EVERYTHING.`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and close your eyes if you like. Think of something you've been searching for that won't show itself: an answer, a decision, the right word. Let go of hunting for the one perfect piece. Picture holding the whole mountain instead: the full situation, with everything in it. Breathe in, and hold it all lightly. Breathe out, and let the answer come when it's ready. The bell holds the time.
The mountain of herbs. A peak in the Himalaya whose healing plants hid from Hanuman, so he lifted the whole mountain and flew it south.
Your line: the mountain of herbs. Today, when you can't find the one piece, step back and take in the whole picture. Day six hundred forty-nine.

howItsDone: Images of Hanuman flying with a mountain on his hand are found in temples, homes and calendars across India, and many Hindus pray to him in times of illness.

match.prompt: the flight north — tap the pairs.

myth: Hanuman lifts the mountain because he's too strong to bother searching
he searches, but the herbs hide themselves.
Valmiki says the herbs hid when they knew someone had come
the demon Kalanemi's trap on the way is in Valmiki
that episode comes from later tellings, such as the Ramcharitmanas.

fork.setup: you're Hanuman, on the herb mountain at night. the four herbs have hidden themselves, and the army is dying. what do you do?
options: lift the whole peak and carry it south.
fork.reveal: he tears off the entire peak, with its trees and herbs, and flies it south, shining like a second sun.

original.note: Sanskrit oṣadhi: a healing plant or herb; the herb mountain is the oṣadhi-parvata.

trapdoor: what you thought: Hanuman carried a mountain to show off his strength.
what it means: the herbs hid, so he brought the whole peak rather than lose the night searching.
what a scholar hears: later tellings add the demon Kalanemi's trap on the way; Valmiki's flight is direct, and the hiding herbs are his.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 74 (Hanuman's flight to the Himalaya; the herbs hide; he lifts the peak)

notes: Sarga number follows the common (vulgate) numbering; confirm.
The mountain Hanuman launches from (in some readings Trikuta or another peak in Lanka): left unnamed.
The herbs hiding themselves, and Hanuman's angry words to the mountain: paraphrased; confirm.
'Shining like a second sun': a paraphrase of Valmiki's image; confirm.
Kalanemi attributed to the Ramcharitmanas (also in the Adhyatma Ramayana); confirm.
In Valmiki this is the first of two herb flights; the second (after Ravana wounds Lakshmana) is mentioned in days 651 and 654.
Audit (10% sample): fixed a line that said Hanuman doesn't waste the night searching right after saying he searches the slopes.
